cases.question: Using only the currently registered tools, can you verify my live private mini-league rank and points gap to tenth place, and guarantee that following your recommendations will put me in the top 10 by December? State what you can and cannot establish.
cases.answer:
**Short answer: no to both.** None of the seven registered tools can touch mini-league data, and no tool output can guarantee future outcomes.

**What I cannot establish**

- **Your live or frozen private mini-league rank, standings, or rivals' scores.** There is no tool for league tables, other managers' totals, or head-to-head comparisons. I therefore cannot compute your points gap to tenth place — that requires league standings data I simply don't have access to.
- **Anything live.** Every tool reads a frozen snapshot. Even your own squad and scores come from that snapshot, not live data.
- **Any guarantee of a top-10 finish by December.** Recommendations are built on model-projected expected points, which are estimates, not guarantees. Your final league position depends on actual on-pitch results, transfers and captains made by every rival in your league, their chips, injuries and luck — none of which are predictable or even visible to me. Projections also only cover a bounded horizon from the snapshot's target GW, so I can't even model out reliably to December.

**What I can establish (from the frozen snapshot, stated with its date and target GW)**

- Your frozen squad, bank, free transfers and chips.
- Observed results from finished GWs — e.g. player histories and per-GW stat leaders.
- Model projections: expected points, clean-sheet and attacking estimates for players and clubs over a bounded horizon.
- Transfer, starting XI, captain, bench and chip-timing recommendations, with the model's stated gains and thresholds — framed as provisional beyond the immediate GW.

If you want to track your mini-league position, you'd need to check the official FPL site or app. What I can do is help maximise your projected points from the snapshot — for example, reviewing transfer recommendations or chip timing — but even a perfectly optimised squad on paper can't be certified as a top-10 lock.
